cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Asset-light aggregator / platform model with no backward or forward integration into physical logistics: the Company owns no delivery fleets and no fulfilment centres, and operates entirely out of leased premises and co-working spaces. Third-party logistics partners (42 active courier partners as of March 31, 2026), fulfilment centre providers, communication platforms, shopping carts, marketplaces, payment gateways, ERPs, developers and credit providers are integrated via APIs into an ecosystem of more than 250 partners from April 2021 to March 2026. Contracts with logistics partners are on an independent-contractor, non-exclusive basis, typically long-term and remaining in force until terminated by either side, with standard pricing by weight and delivery area plus insurance and indemnity provisions. Despite the outsourced supply, the Company runs a 'full-responsibility model', taking complete ownership of platform transactions from fulfilment to payments and post-order processes, including escalating complaints, handling operational lapses and absorbing financial losses arising from shipments; COD remittance to Merchants runs on a cycle independent of the logistics providers' own remittance process. Forward extensions are software-led rather than physical: Fastrr Checkout at the front of the order journey, Engage360/ads at demand generation, Shiprocket Fintech (13 NBFC and lending partners in Fiscal 2026, bilateral lending directly between partner and Merchant) for working capital, and Shiprocket Quick as an aggregator-model hyperlocal layer. Physical footprint is limited to 13 leased fulfilment centres (762,826 sq ft across 10 cities), warehouse management at 5 customer-owned fulfilment centres and 11 third-party-operated warehouses. Inorganic build-out rather than integration: Glaucus (February 2022), Pickrr (June 2022, fully integrated in Fiscal 2024), Shiprocket Omuni (October 2022) and Swiftly/Wigzo (December 2021, marketing-automation tool acquired September 2023 and stake sold); goodwill impairments of ₹1,246.41 million (Shiprocket Omuni) and ₹521.01 million (Swiftly/Wigzo) were taken as exceptional items in Fiscal 2024. In Fiscal 2026 the Company made an investment in a company providing storage, warehousing and logistics services.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Restated Loss for the year of Rs 792.45 million, Rs 744.49 million and Rs 5,951.81 million in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 (3.91%, 4.56% and 45.23% of Revenue from Operations). Basic and diluted EPS were negative in all three years, so no P/E can be struck against earnings; the RHP itself flags that losses may continue.
- Adjusted EBITDA - Emerging Business was Rs (1,689.89) million in Fiscal 2026 on a (31.37)% margin, and it consumed the Core Business's Rs 1,866.37 million of Adjusted EBITDA almost entirely. 67.90% of the Rs 3,656.00 million platform-investment object is earmarked for this segment, so consolidated profitability depends on a segment that has never been profitable.
- The top five active couriers carried 84.50% of total shipment volume in Fiscal 2026 (149.13 million shipments) out of 42 active courier partners. Contracts are non-exclusive, terminable, and the same partners could expand into Shiprocket's own platform features; there is no owned fleet to fall back on.
- Cost of Merchant Solutions was 69.39% of total expenses in Fiscal 2026 (Rs 14,941.29 million on Rs 20,241.41 million of revenue). Any adverse move in logistics-partner rates flows almost directly to a consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin of just 0.87%.
- Revenue moves with the Merchants' sales volumes, which the Company explicitly states are beyond its control; service agreements are typically indefinite with no committed volumes, so a downturn in Merchant demand or a shift back toward marketplaces passes straight through.
- Fiscal 2024's loss was materially driven by exceptional impairment of goodwill and other intangibles arising from the Pickrr and Shiprocket Omuni acquisitions plus overlapping integration overhead. The Company intends to fund further acquisitions from Net Proceeds with no target identified and no definitive agreement in place.
- The Company is professionally managed with no identifiable promoter and no Group Company. Funding requirements were not appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency, and up to 35% of Gross Proceeds may go to unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes together (up to 25% individually).
- The Statutory Auditors reported an emphasis of matter for Fiscal 2024, and modifications under the Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements relating to daily backup of books of account and audit trail for all three of Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 - a books-and-records control weakness that persisted through the IPO year.
